<p></p>

<p>This document describes how to configure and use Gemini Code Assist
agent mode as a pair programmer in your integrated development environment
(IDE).</p>

<p>With agent mode, you can do any of the following and more:</p>

<ul>
<li>Ask questions about your code.</li>
<li>Use context and built-in tools to improve generated content.</li>
<li>Configure MCP servers to extend the agent&#39;s abilities.</li>
<li>Get solutions to complex tasks with multiple steps.</li>
<li>Generate code from design documents, issues, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">TODO</code> comments.</li>
<li>Control the agent behavior by commenting on, editing, and approving plans
and tool use during execution.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="limitations" data-text="Limitations" tabindex="-1">Limitations</h2>

<p>Some features of <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/chat-overview">standard Gemini Code Assist chat</a>
might not be available in agent mode or might work differently than they do in
standard chat.</p>

<p>Recitation is not available in agent mode. While in agent mode, Gemini
doesn&#39;t <a href="/gemini/docs/discover/works#how-when-gemini-cites-sources">cite sources</a> and you can&#39;t
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#disable_code_suggestions_that_match_cited_sources">disable code suggestions that match cited sources</a>.</p>

<h2 id="before-you-begin" data-text="Before you begin" tabindex="-1">Before you begin</h2>

<ol>
<li><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini">Set up Gemini Code Assist</a>.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="use-agent-mode" data-text="Use agent mode" tabindex="-1">Use agent mode</h2>

<p>In agent mode, you can ask Gemini to complete high-level goals and
complex tasks.</p>

<p>To get the most out of agent mode, follow
<a href="/gemini/docs/discover/write-prompts">prompting best practices</a> and provide as much detail as
possible.</p>
<aside class="caution"><strong>Caution:</strong><span> There isn&#39;t an option to undo changes made to resources outside your
IDE in agent mode, so be careful where you use it.</span></aside>
<p>To switch to agent mode:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li>To open the Gemini Code Assist chat, in the activity bar of your
IDE, click <span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span>
<strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong>.</li>
<li>Click the <strong>Agent</strong> toggle to enter agent mode. The toggle is highlighted
when toggled to agent mode and grey when in regular chat.</li>
<li>In the Gemini Code Assist chat, enter your prompt.</li>
</ol>

<p>Gemini gives you a response to your prompt, or requests permission
to use a tool.</p>

<p>To stop the agent, click <span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">stop</span><strong>Stop</strong>.</p>

<p>To use the standard Gemini Code Assist chat, click
<span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">add</span><strong>New chat</strong> to create a new
chat.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li>Click <span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini</strong>
in the tool window bar. Sign in if prompted to do so.</li>
<li>Select the <strong>Agent</strong> tab.</li>
<li>Describe the task you want the agent to perform.</li>
<li><p>As the agent goes through the steps to accomplish the task, you&#39;ll have the
option to review and approve any changes.</p></li>
<li><p>Optional: To automatically approve changes, select
<span class="google-symbols">settings</span> <strong>Agent options</strong> and
click the checkbox next to <strong>Auto-approve changes</strong>.</p>
<aside class="caution"><strong>Caution:</strong><span> The agent has access to your machine&#39;s file system and terminal
actions as well as any tools you&#39;ve configured for use. Be extremely
careful where and when you auto-approve changes.</span></aside></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="configure-tools-for-agent-mode" data-text="Configure tools for agent mode" tabindex="-1">Configure tools for agent mode</h2>

<p><em>Tools</em> are a broad category of services that an agent can use for context and
actions in its response to your prompt. Some example tools are built-in tools
like grep and file read or write, local or remote Model Context Protocol (MCP)
servers and their executable functions, or bespoke service implementations.</p>

<h3 id="control-built-in-tool-use" data-text="Control built-in tool use" tabindex="-1">Control built-in tool use</h3>

<p>Agent mode has access to your built-in tools like file search, file read, file
write, terminal commands, and more.</p>








<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_1" data-text="VS Code" tabindex="-1">VS Code</h3><p>You can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">coreTools</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">excludeTools</code> settings to control which tools
Gemini has access to in agent mode.</p>

<dl>
<dt><code translate="no" dir="ltr">coreTools</code></dt>
<dd>Lets you specify a list of tools that you want to be available to
the model. You can also specify command-specific restrictions for tools that
support it. For example—adding the following to your
Gemini settings JSON will only allow the shell <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ls -l</code> command to
be executed:<code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;coreTools&quot;: [&quot;ShellTool(ls -l)&quot;]</code>.</dd>
<dt><code translate="no" dir="ltr">excludeTools</code></dt>
<dd>Lets you specify a list of tools that you don&#39;t want to be available to the
model. You can also specify command-specific restrictions for tools that
support it. For example—adding the following to your Gemini
settings JSON will block the use of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">rm -rf</code> command:
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;excludeTools&quot;: [&quot;ShellTool(rm -rf)&quot;]</code>.</dd>
</dl>

<p>A tool listed in both <code translate="no" dir="ltr">excludeTools</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">coreTools</code> is excluded.</p>

<p>To configure the built-in tools available in agent mode, do the following:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open your Gemini settings JSON located in
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">~/.gemini/settings.json</code> where <code translate="no" dir="ltr">~</code> is your home directory.</li>
<li><p>To restrict agent tool use to a list of approved tools, add the
following line to your Gemini settings JSON:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"coreTools"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME_1</var>,<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME_2</var>"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Replace <var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME_1</code></var> and
<var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME_2</code></var> with the names of the
<a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/">built-in tools</a> you want the
agent to have access to.</p>

<p>You can list as many built-in tools as you want.
By default all built-in tools are available to the agent.</p></li>
<li><p>To restrict agent tool use to specific tool commands, add the
following line to your Gemini settings JSON:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"coreTools"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME</var>(<var translate="no">COMMAND</var>)"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Replace the following:</p>

<ul>
<li><var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME</code></var>: the name of the built-in tool</li>
<li><var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">COMMAND</code></var>: the name of the built-in tool command
you want the agent to be able to use.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>To exclude a tool from agent use, add the following line to your
Gemini settings JSON:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"excludeTools"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME_1</var>,<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME_2</var>"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Replace <var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME_1</code></var> and
<var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME_2</code></var> with the names of the
<a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/">built-in tools</a> you want to exclude from agent use.</p></li>
<li><p>To exclude a tool command from agent use, add the following line to your
Gemini settings JSON:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"excludeTools"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">TOOL_NAME</var>(<var translate="no">COMMAND</var>)"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Replace the following:</p>

<ul>
<li><var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">TOOL_NAME</code></var>: the name of the built-in tool</li>
<li><var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">COMMAND</code></var>: the name of the built-in tool command
you want to exclude from agent use.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>

<p>For more information about the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">coreTools</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">excludeTools</code> configuration
settings, see the
<a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/configuration/">Gemini CLI configuration documentation</a>.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_1" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>This feature isn&#39;t supported in Gemini Code Assist for IntelliJ or
other JetBrains IDEs.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="configure-mcp-servers" data-text="Configure MCP servers" tabindex="-1">Configure MCP servers</h3>
<aside class="caution"><strong>Caution:</strong><span> MCP servers can run arbitrary code with the permissions available to
your user account. Make sure you trust the source of any MCP servers you use.</span></aside>
<p>The following instructions show how to make MCP servers available for use in
agent mode in your IDE. After you make an MCP server available,
Gemini Code Assist automatically decides when and how to use the
server tools contained within that MCP server.</p>


<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_2" data-text="VS Code" tabindex="-1">VS Code</h3><p>To make MCP servers available for use in agent mode, add the configuration for
each server in your Gemini settings JSON file, according each
server&#39;s documentation.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> You can&#39;t use the command palette to install MCP servers for agent mode.
You must add MCP servers to your Gemini settings JSON file.</span></aside>
<ol>
<li>Install any dependencies required by the MCP servers you are adding.</li>
<li>Open your Gemini settings JSON file, located at
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">~/.gemini/settings.json</code> where <code translate="no" dir="ltr">~</code> is your home directory.</li>
<li><p>Configure each local or remote MCP server in the Gemini settings
JSON file, according to each server&#39;s instructions.</p>

<p>The following example Gemini settings JSON file configures two
remote Cloudflare MCP servers, a remote GitLab MCP server, and a local
GitHub MCP server for use with Gemini Code Assist in VS Code.</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"mcpServers"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"github"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"-y"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"env"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"ghp_example_personal_access_token12345"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"gitlab"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://your-gitlab-instance.com/api/v4/mcp"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"cloudflare-observability"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/sse"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"cloudflare-bindings"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://bindings.mcp.cloudflare.com/sse"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p></li>
<li><p>Open the command palette and select <strong>Developer: Reload Window</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Your configured MCP servers are available for the agent to use in agent mode.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_2" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>To make MCP servers available for use in agent mode, add the configuration for
each server in a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> file and place the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> file in the
<a href="https://intellij-support.jetbrains.com/hc/en-us/articles/206544519-Directories-used-by-the-IDE-to-store-settings-caches-plugins-and-logs">configuration directory</a> for your IDE.</p>

<ol>
<li>Install any dependencies required by the MCP servers you are adding.</li>
<li>Create a file named <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> in your IDE&#39;s
<a href="https://intellij-support.jetbrains.com/hc/en-us/articles/206544519-Directories-used-by-the-IDE-to-store-settings-caches-plugins-and-logs">configuration directory</a>.</li>
<li><p>Configure each local or remote MCP server in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> file,
according to each server&#39;s instructions.</p>

<p>The following example <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> file configures two remote Cloudflare MCP
servers, a remote GitLab MCP server, and a local GitHub MCP server for use
with Gemini Code Assist in IntelliJ.</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"mcpServers"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"github"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"-y"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"env"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"ghp_example_personal_access_token12345"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"gitlab"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://your-gitlab-instance.com/api/v4/mcp"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"cloudflare-observability"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/sse"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"cloudflare-bindings"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"npx"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"mcp-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://bindings.mcp.cloudflare.com/sse"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Your configured MCP servers are available for the agent to use in agent mode.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h4 id="mcp-server-authn" data-text="MCP server authentication" tabindex="-1">MCP server authentication</h4>

<p>Some MCP servers require authentication. Follow the server documentation to
create any required user tokens, and then specify them appropriately. Typically,
you specify authentication tokens for local servers using the appropriate
server-specific environment variable, and you specify authentication tokens for
remote servers using the HTTP <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Authorization</code> header.</p>




<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_3" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>For MCP servers that require authentication, you can add them to your
Gemini settings JSON.</p>

<p>The following example shows how to specify a personal access token for the
GitHub local and remote MCP servers:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"mcpServers"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"github-remote"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"httpUrl"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"headers"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"Authorization"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"Bearer <var translate="no">ACCESS_TOKEN</var>"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">},</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"github-local"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"/Users/username/code/github-mcp-server/cmd/github-mcp-server/github-mcp-server"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"stdio"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"env"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">ACCESS_TOKEN</var>"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Where <var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ACCESS_TOKEN</code></var> is the user&#39;s access token.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_3" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>For MCP servers that require authentication, you can add them to your
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">mcp.json</code> file.</p>

<p>The following example adds a personal access token for the GitHub local server:</p>

<p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"mcpServers"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"github-local"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"command"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"/Users/username/code/github-mcp-server/cmd/github-mcp-server/github-mcp-server"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"args"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"stdio"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"env"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"<var translate="no">ACCESS_TOKEN</var>"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
</p>

<p>Where <var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ACCESS_TOKEN</code></var> is the user&#39;s access token.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="create-context-file" data-text="Create a context file" tabindex="-1">Create a context file</h3>

<p>Context allows an agent to generate better responses for a given prompt. Context
can be taken from files in your IDE, files in your local system folders, tool
responses, and your prompt details. For more information, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/agent-mode#agent-mode-context">Agent mode context</a>.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_4" data-text=" VS Code" tabindex="-1"> VS Code</h3><ol>
<li><p>Create a file named <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GEMINI.md</code> in a location that matches the scope you
want the context to apply to. The following table details the locations for
context files for different scopes:</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Scope</th>
<th>Location</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>All your projects</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">~/.gemini/GEMINI.md</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A specific project</td>
<td>Your working directory or any parent directories up to either your project root (identified by a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.git</code> folder) or your home directory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A specific component, module, or sub-section of a project</td>
<td>Subdirectories of your working directory.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p>The agent&#39;s memory system is created by loading context files from
multiple locations. Context from more specific files, like those for
specific components or modules, overrides or supplements content from
more general context files like the global context file at
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">~/.gemini/GEMINI.md</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>Write any rules, style guide information, or context that you want the
agent to use in Markdown and save the file. For more information, see
the <a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/">example context file on GitHub</a>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>The agent includes the information in your context file along with any prompts
you send to it.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_4" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>Create a file named either <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GEMINI.md</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">AGENT.md</code> at the root of your
project.</p></li>
<li><p>Write any rules, style guide information, or context that you want the
agent to use in Markdown and save the file.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>The agent includes the information in your context file along with any prompts
you send to it. You can also add context by including a file manually with the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">@</code><var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">FILENAME</code></var> syntax where
<var translate="no"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">FILENAME</code></var> is the name of the file with contextual
information you want to include.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="use-commands" data-text="Use commands" tabindex="-1">Use commands</h2>



<p>Slash <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/</code> commands let you quickly run commands similar to commands in a
terminal window.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_5" data-text="VS Code" tabindex="-1">VS Code</h3><p>You can use the following built-in Gemini CLI commands in agent
mode:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">/tools</code>: Displays a list of tools that are available in your agent mode
session.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">/mcp</code>: Lists configured Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, their
connection status, server details, and available tools.</li>
</ul>

<p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">/deploy</code>: Deploys a web application to Cloud Run. This
Gemini CLI-based <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/gemini-cli-custom-slash-commands">custom command</a> uses the
Cloud Run Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to
build, containerize, push, configure, and return a public URL for your
application. You must have Cloud Run enabled in your Google Cloud
project and install the
<a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-run-mcp?tab=readme-ov-file#use-as-a-gemini-cli-extension">Cloud Run MCP server as a Gemini extension</a>
to use this command.</li>
</ul>

</p>

<p>For more information on Gemini CLI commands, see
<a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/commands/">Gemini CLI Commands</a> and
<a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/custom-commands/">Gemini custom commands</a>. Note that not
all Gemini CLI commands are available in agent mode.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_5" data-text="IntelliJ" tabindex="-1">IntelliJ</h3><p>This feature isn&#39;t supported in Gemini Code Assist for IntelliJ or
other JetBrains IDEs.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="yolo-mode" data-text="Always allow agent actions" tabindex="-1">Always allow agent actions</h2>

<p>You can automatically allow all agent actions.</p>
<aside class="warning"><strong>Warning:</strong><span> The agent has access to your machine&#39;s file system and terminal actions
as well as any tools you&#39;ve configured for use. Be extremely careful where and
when you automatically allow agent actions.</span></aside>
<p>To automatically allow all agent actions:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_6" data-text="VS Code" tabindex="-1">VS Code</h3><p>Use yolo mode to automatically allow all agent actions. Yolo mode can only be
used in a <a href="https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/workspace-trust">trusted workspace</a>.</p>

<p>To configure yolo mode:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Open your VS Code user settings JSON file:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open the <strong>Command palette</strong> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">ctrl</code>/<code translate="no" dir="ltr">command</code> + <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Shift</code> + <code translate="no" dir="ltr">P</code>).</li>
<li>Select <strong>Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)</strong>.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>Add the following to your VS Code user settings JSON file:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-c1">//other settings...</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"geminicodeassist.agentYoloMode"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kc">true</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-c1">//other settings...</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>Open the command palette and select <strong>Developer: Reload Window</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Agent mode uses yolo mode, and won&#39;t ask for permission before taking actions
when you send it a prompt. When using a
<a href="https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editing/workspaces/workspace-trust#_restricted-mode">restricted workspace</a> the agent will prompt before
taking actions regardless of this setting.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_6" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>To automatically approve changes, in the Gemini chat agent tab,
select <span class="google-symbols">settings</span> <strong>Agent options</strong> and then
click the checkbox next to <strong>Auto-approve changes</strong>.</p>

<p>Agent mode automatically approves all requests, and won&#39;t ask for permission
before taking actions when you send it a prompt.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="additional" data-text="Additional prompts" tabindex="-1">Additional prompts</h2>

<p>Try out the following prompts with your own information:</p>

<ul>
<li>&quot;What does this repository do? Help me understand the architecture.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;What does this [class/function] do?&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Add a feature to this codebase - &quot;[link-or-path-to-codebase]&quot;.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Refactor function [A] and [B] to use the common method [C].&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Fix the GitHub issue [link-to-github-issue].&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Build an application to do [goal] with a UI that lets the user do [task] in
the [environment].&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Migrate library versions in this repository from [X] to [Y].&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Optimize performance of this Go code so that it runs faster.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Use [name-of-API] to build out this feature.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;Implement an algorithm to do [x], [Y], and [Z].&quot;</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="api-key" data-text="Optional: Use an API Key" tabindex="-1">Optional: Use an API Key</h2>

<p>Gemini Code Assist includes different daily
<a href="/gemini/docs/quotas#quotas-for-agent-mode-gemini-cli">quotas</a> for agentic
features, depending on the tier you&#39;re in.</p>

<p>If you&#39;ve exhausted your daily quota for Gemini Code Assist
agent mode, you can continue to use the service by providing an API key. You can
use either a <a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key">Gemini API key</a> or a
<a href="/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/start/api-keys">Vertex AI API key</a>.</p>

<p>To add your API key:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Navigate to your IDE&#39;s settings.</p></li>
<li><p>Open the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">settings.json</code> file.</p></li>
<li><p>Add the following line, replacing <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">YOUR_KEY</var></code> with your
API key:</p>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;geminicodeassist.geminiApiKey&quot;: &quot;<var translate="no">YOUR_KEY</var>&quot;</code></p></li>
</ol>

<h2 id="whats-next" data-text="What's next" tabindex="-1">What's next</h2>

<ul>
<li>Read the <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview">Gemini Code Assist overview</a>.</li>
<li>Explore some <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/examples">example MCP servers</a>.</li>
<li>Find more <a href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers">MCP servers on GitHub</a>.</li>
<li><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#leave_feedback">Send feedback from your IDE</a>.</li>
</ul>
